content.title: About
content.content: Corn fritter is a crunchy snack made from whole corn kernels that are deep‑fried or air‑fried until golden. It has a light sweet corn flavor and a satisfying crisp texture. Fritters are commonly enjoyed as a snack, topping for salads, soups, or as a crunchy element in Asian dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn is one of the most widely cultivated crops worldwide, grown in over 150 countries.
Corn fritters originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a way to preserve surplus harvests.
Corn belongs to the grass family and is a close relative of sorghum, rice, and wheat.
There are several varieties of corn fritters: sweet, salted, spiced, and flavored with cheese or herbs.
Corn fritters are often used as a gluten‑free alternative to bread crumbs.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Corn provides fiber that supports healthy digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in corn help protect the eyes from oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Fritters contain thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Provides magnesium and potassium
items.content: These minerals support muscle function, nerve signaling, and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Low in fat when air‑fried
items.content: Compared with many fried snacks, air‑fried corn fritters contain relatively little fat.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Corn fritters can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salted versions may contain significant amounts of sodium, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Potential acrylamide formation
items.content: Deep‑frying at very high temperatures can create acrylamide and other potentially harmful compounds.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Corn fritters can be enjoyed straight from the bag, tossed into salads, added to soups, used in tacos, or crushed as a crunchy coating for fish or chicken. They are convenient for on‑the‑go snacking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fritters in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to prevent rancidity. Follow the expiration date printed on the package.
